stages.name: Interest
stages.job: Create enough qualified attention from the right kind of customer

stages.name: Intent
stages.job: Turn that attention into real, progressing opportunities

stages.name: Commitment
stages.job: Convert them into paying customers, with predictable timing

stages.name: Value
stages.job: Keep customers, and grow the value of the ones you have

root_causes.name: Proposition
root_causes.asks: Is the proposition, value and business case sharp enough?

root_causes.name: People
root_causes.asks: Are the right people, with the right judgement and accountability, owning it?

root_causes.name: Process
root_causes.asks: Is there a defined, evidenced way of working that can be inspected?

root_causes.name: Repeatability
root_causes.asks: Is what works captured, codified and reused rather than reinvented?

arithmetic: stage = mean(the 4 cells in that row)
rootCause = mean(that cause across all 4 stages)

motion_aware.principle: The construct is fixed for every company. The question wording and the indicator each question asks about vary by business model and maturity.

motions.name: B2B subscription software and digital services
B2B physical product, hardware and deeptech
B2C physical product, direct to consumer and e-commerce

maturity_levels.name: Pre-revenue
maturity_levels.asks: Is there evidence anyone will pay, found by a means that does not depend on the founder alone?

maturity_levels.name: Early revenue
maturity_levels.asks: Did it work more than once, for reasons you can name and repeat?

maturity_levels.name: Scaling
maturity_levels.asks: Does it work without the founder in the room, and does it survive more volume?

motion_aware.comparability: Scores are comparable across motions because the construct, scales and arithmetic are identical. Peer benchmarking is only valid within one motion at one maturity level.
